episodes.title: Everything You Need to Know About AI Tokens (Operator's Cut, with Nufar Gaspar)
episodes.reason: Podcast hosts (itunes.apple.com, feeds.megaphone.fm, podscan.fm, pca.st, aidailybrief.ai, podcasts.apple.com) all still 403 at the proxy, so this is a search-coverage extraction, not a transcript. Corroborated consistently across independent WebSearch queries (same phrasing recurred: 'cost per successful task', 'tokens that spin', 'choose the right models', 'protect the experimentation that creates real value', 'four eras of token consumption', 'Claudenomics and $500M bills'), which is a strong signal it's real show-notes text and not a hallucinated summary. Extracted 2 tactics: cost-per-successful-task accounting, and capping unproductive agentic retries ('tokens that spin'). Did not extract 'choose the right model' or 'protect experimentation' as standalone tactics — the material available on those was too thin to make concrete without inventing detail. A distinct 'August 3' episode also turned up in search, but two independent WebSearch queries gave contradictory content for it (one described a revenue/stock-drawdown recap, the other described an Astra-model/Deepseek/Amazon news recap) — unreliable enough that no ledger entry was recorded for it rather than guess. Direct episode URL unconfirmed; only the show's main page was reachable-ish in search results.

episodes.title: 6 Questions Every Enterprise Has to Answer About AI
episodes.reason: iTunes lookup, the feed, and every podcast/show-notes host (pod.link, aidailybrief.ai, Spotify episode page, Apple Podcasts, Pocket Casts, podnews.net) returned 403 at the proxy — WebFetch is blocked broadly in this environment, not just the listed podcast hosts. WebSearch surfaced only that NLW recaps 'six questions' from a KPMG symposium (enterprise AI shifting from 'if' to 'how'), with four themes corroborated (token budgets, workforce enablement, business-model change, adaptive systems) but not the actual questions or NLW's mechanism for each. Building a ready-to-paste artifact from fragments would mean inventing content the episode may or may not actually contain. Promising — worth a manual listen once the network policy allows transcript/show-notes access.
